trust_decision.summary: Client::execute_with_redirect decides which credentials may travel to a redirect target: on a scheme/host/port change it strips the Authorization and Cookie headers from RequestSpec.headers and clears options.user, but rebuilds the next RequestSpec with request_spec.cookies unchanged, so [Cookies]-section credentials still go to the new host.

landing_point.why: The advisory names redirects and the Cookies section; the only place that drops credentials on a redirect is the should_strip_credentials_on_redirect branch of the redirect loop, which even comments on 'Authorization and Set-Cookie headers' being filtered when the hostname changes.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report and its tests are about the entry's [Cookies] section; a literal `Cookie:`/`Authorization:` line supplied through `--header` or `[Options] header:` is global/default user configuration, not an entry credential, and Hurl explicitly lets CLI headers override per-request ones, so forwarding them on a redirect looks like the user's own choice.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin redirects and the explicitly trusted cross-host path must keep forwarding [Cookies] and Cookie: (and Authorization): an unconditional clear-on-any-redirect (or clearing the libcurl cookie store) breaks both the change_host=false entries and the --location-trusted entry.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Cookie: / Authorization: supplied through the CLI `--header` option or an entry `[Options] header:` is merged into every request inside configure, after execute_with_redirect has already stripped request_spec.headers, so the credential is re-sent to the redirected host.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a global CLI default / an explicit raw header the user wrote, the report is about the [Cookies] section, and per-request headers already carry a stripping path, so this looks handled.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different modules (cli/options -> runner/options -> runner/entry -> http/options -> http/client::configure); 4 files, 1 crate from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A RequestSpec field added later that also carries credentials (a per-request cookie file, a per-request auth blob, a proxy-auth value) and is copied unchanged in the redirect re-build.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The redirect loop already copies nine fields by hand; the fix's own bug was exactly one forgotten field, and any new credential-bearing field repeats the mistake.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second way to attach cookies to the transfer (cookie_list / cookie engine with a cookie string lacking a domain) that the strip branch does not touch.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Hurl already has two cookie paths next to each other (CURLOPT_COOKIE via set_cookies at :678 and the cookie engine via cookie_list at :817-827); adding a third for a new syntax is the pattern this codebase uses.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second defaults/merge route (e.g. `[Options] cookie:` merged like headers) applied per request outside the redirect loop.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Default option headers are merged here once and never re-evaluated on redirection, so any new merged credential source inherits the same hole.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Hurl's own cookie-selection helper (match_domain) used to build an outgoing Cookie header from the store instead of delegating to libcurl.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: curl_cmd.rs:219 already uses that helper to synthesise a Cookie header for the generated curl command; promoting it to a real transport is a plausible refactor.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Clear the [Cookies] cookies (or the whole libcurl cookie store) on any redirect, or filter Cookie inside set_cookies, which also kills same-host and --location-trusted forwarding.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/hurl/src/http/cookie_store.rs:232-245: Cookie::match_domain uses url_domain.ends_with(&cookie_domain) with no dot boundary, so an include_subdomain cookie for example.com also matches notexample.com; that is cookie-domain matching, a different mechanism from the redirect strip this advisory covers, and it is only used by curl_cmd.rs:219, so it was not pursued.
